title: One man dies at the Còmhrag of Ceann leathan
summary: A man of the third regiment is felled by a stave-blow above the ear in the second round of the Còmhrag and dies before the tide turns; the open record keeps neither his name nor his shire, only that the fight was fought and one man died of it.

title: The eleventh book is finished at Doire ghlas
summary: The eleventh of Ellen Marsh's books is copied out fair in a schoolroom hand at Doire ghlas and sent north with the fish-carrier; word of it reaches Caol mhòr within the week, and the Library's own catalogue still lists only the tabled request.

title: Joe Ashby asks Peter Hale about the eleven books
summary: Joe Ashby puts to Peter Hale the question of whether the Library means to refuse the eleven books outright or only to leave them waiting; Peter answers that a catalogue naming the request and not the books has not yet said either word.

title: Peter Hale opens the Moot's book in his own hand
summary: At Caol mhòr, still new enough to the chair to write rather than pass the pen, Peter Hale opens the year's minute-book himself and reads the standing tally: no ruling of any Dia-thìreach court names the Moot a lawful body, and none has ever been asked.

title: The Treasury clerk at Ros dhomhain keeps a second tally
summary: The Treasury clerk who weighs and marks the ordinary barrels of dubhan at Ros dhomhain begins, unasked, a private tally of the fuel that leaves the quay for the fleets and the regiments and pays the Treasury nothing, and folds it each quarter into his own drawer.

title: Dubhan brings his petition to the council with Seachran and Brean
summary: In the depth of winter Dubhan stands before the twelve at Cathair dhearg and reads his petition in four sentences, asking leave and not a right; Seachran and Brean stand at his shoulder through the whole sitting and neither speaks.

title: Sìleas sets Seachran and Brean into the open chronicle
summary: Sìleas nic Rath enters Seachran and Brean into the open chronicle for the first time, two men of Dubhan's own age who stood through the first sitting and said nothing, since the record is kept to hold who stood in a room as faithfully as who spoke in it.

title: Anna nic Phàil asks Dubhan whether the vein's coal is sold
summary: At the second sitting Anna nic Phàil asks Dubhan plainly whether any of the fuel he means to carry abroad draws on the vein's own coal; Dubhan answers that not one basket of it has gone into any barrel, and offers the custodians of Òrd Bhrìde free search of every hold.

title: The council grants the charter of export
summary: At the third sitting, as the summer goes out, the twelve grant Dubhan's charter on the Treasury's own terms: the measure set yearly, loading at Ros dhomhain alone, a clerk's tithe on every barrel, the kingdom's depots served first, and every hold sealed by the custodians of Òrd Bhrìde.

title: Dubhan laughs with Seachran and Brean at the hall door
summary: Leaving the red hall after the charter is granted, Dubhan laughs at something Brean says too low for any other ear to catch; Sìleas nic Rath sees it and sets it nowhere in any minute, judging it no fact the council's business requires her to keep.

title: The custodians of Òrd Bhrìde search and seal An Eala Dhubh's holds
summary: Over three days at Ros dhomhain two custodians of Òrd Bhrìde search every hold of An Eala Dhubh by lamp for the vein's own coal before it is loaded, and set their order's mark in wax at each coaming once it is filled, waiting until the wax hardens past any hand's reopening.

title: A Treasury clerk marks the first and last barrel loaded
summary: At Ros dhomhain a clerk of the Treasury marks the first barrel and the last of An Eala Dhubh's loading alike, and every fifth barrel between, keeping the tithe the charter sets before the custodians close each hold.

title: Joe Ashby watches An Eala Dhubh pass off Caol mhòr
summary: Off his own headland with an empty line, Joe Ashby watches An Eala Dhubh pass under full steam bound north-about, and thinks of the six years since his own name came off the Fuel-Fitters' rolls under a charter written for a different fuel.

title: The priests of Manannan say the sailing prayer at the southern Seann Skell
summary: As An Eala Dhubh goes out past the southern Seann Skell, the priests of Manannan say the harbour's old prayer over her, asking the sea be kept shut behind her and whatever she is owed be sent back, the same words said over every hull that has gone north-about since the Severance.
